We are TEAM RELIQ, passionate innovators in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project uncovers the stories of human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars, highlighting their scientific and historical significance. We welcome collaborators skilled in programming, UI/UX design, 3D visualization, research, and storytelling.

Our motto: “Forgotten on Worlds. Remembered by Humanity.” 🚀
summary:
FORGOTTEN WORLDS: An Interactive Archaeological Archive of Humanity Beyond Earth

Humanity has explored the Moon and Mars for decades, leaving behind spacecraft, rovers, scientific instruments, landing systems, and countless traces of exploration. But what happened to these objects after their missions ended?

FORGOTTEN WORLDS transforms this forgotten history into an interactive digital archaeological archive. Our project brings together documented lunar and Martian artifacts through immersive planetary exploration, mission timelines, searchable artifact records, scientific imagery, and interactive storytelling.

Users can discover Apollo landing hardware, lunar scientific instruments, Mars rovers, landers, and discarded components from robotic landing systems. By connecting historical missions with NASA imagery and planetary science resources, we reveal the scientific and historical significance of these objects.

Our goal is to preserve the stories of humanity's exploration beyond Earth and make planetary science accessible, engaging, and meaningful for everyone.

Forgotten on Worlds. Remembered by Humanity.
details:
FORGOTTEN WORLDS – Project Details

1. Problem Statement

Decades of lunar and Martian exploration have left behind numerous human-made objects, including landers, rovers, scientific instruments, landing stages, parachutes, heat shields and other spacecraft components.

Although these objects represent significant scientific and engineering achievements, their stories, purposes, locations and present conditions are scattered across mission archives, scientific publications and historical records. This makes it difficult for students, educators and the general public to understand what humanity has left behind on other worlds.

2. Our Solution

FORGOTTEN WORLDS is an interactive digital archaeological archive designed to document and explore humanity's physical legacy on the Moon and Mars.

It transforms scientific mission records and historical information into an engaging planetary exploration experience. Instead of simply displaying mission information, our platform allows users to discover individual artifacts, understand their purposes, explore their histories and learn why they matter.

3. Key Features

• Interactive Moon and Mars Exploration: Explore planetary environments and discover documented mission sites and artifacts.

• Artifact Discovery Archive: Search and filter lunar and Martian objects based on their missions, categories, years and operational status.

• Mission Timeline: Discover the history of planetary exploration through important missions and milestones.

• Landing Debris Exploration: Understand how spacecraft landing systems separate into components, including heat shields, parachutes, backshells and descent stages.

• Scientific Storytelling: Learn about lunar experiments, laser retroreflectors, Mars rovers, landers and other scientific equipment.

• Mission Images and References: Connect historical discoveries with authentic NASA imagery and scientific resources.

• Planetary Preservation: Understand how the Moon's and Mars' environments influence the preservation of human-made objects.

5. Creativity and Innovation

Our main innovation is presenting planetary exploration through the perspective of space archaeology. We connect scientific information with interactive discovery and historical storytelling, allowing visitors to see abandoned equipment not as ordinary debris, but as evidence of humanity's technological progress.

6. Intended Impact

FORGOTTEN WORLDS aims to make planetary science more accessible, encourage curiosity about space exploration, preserve the historical significance of planetary missions and inspire future generations to understand the scientific legacy humanity is creating beyond Earth.

Our vision is to turn forgotten spacecraft and equipment into a meaningful digital record of human exploration.

FORGOTTEN ON WORLDS. REMEMBERED BY HUMANITY.
